<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**55** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`, `owner_id (literal, 46 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf9115e837647a8fa118abf300eaf203ff53dea8` — the merge of head `977e416ad0a93972e380cd100c297e191a878c73` into base `3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf9115e837647a8fa118abf300eaf203ff53dea8 && git checkout cf9115e837647a8fa118abf300eaf203ff53dea8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c 977e416ad0a93972e380cd100c297e191a878c73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c && git merge --no-ff 977e416ad0a93972e380cd100c297e191a878c73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3e4d531d8ff39985ad044067b8d550e4af30799c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · REWORK (2 must-fix)** · Head-sha: `fb4501686231790f6339cb12d9b6a7d1ef0f1dde` · card #35145 (`Fixes #35145`, PR 2 of 2) · read 2026-11-18T17:08Z

Net diff against merge base `ec227fc7b18`: 8 files, +1185 / -8. `query_records` gains `expand` (forward references, one level, at most 3), and `get_record` gains `related` (child lists, at most 3, capped at 20 rows each).

### Must-fix

- **M1. One new sentence in the tool text is false for a case the PR itself describes.** The `query_records` description ends its `expand` sentence with "a field whose object you may not read refuses the call". Per this PR's own acceptance note and the engine's expansion path, only the MCP read guard's refusal refuses the call. A target the engine does not expand for the caller (for example, one the caller holds no object permission on) answers the stored id on the row, and the call succeeds. The model reads this text, so it must say what the tool does.
  - Reword it so the guard's refusal is what refuses the call, and so an unexpanded target keeps its id.
  - Add one pin for that case. The CRM example has one ready: `crm_activity.contact` points at `crm_contact`, which the dogfood member may not read. Expanding it should answer the call, with the field holding its stored id.
- **M2. CI is red at this head:** `PR-body guards` reports that the PR closes #35145 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/issue-35145-mcp-related-read`. Post a claim amendment on the card that names this branch, then re-run the guard.

### Against the card

- **`Fixes` is right.** PR 1 (#35199) carried `latestPer` and the card's "each X with its latest Y" pin. The card's second done-when clause, that the ask cards carry both kinds, names #35113 as its carrier, and #35113's scope already lists `join` and `owner_latest`. This PR carries the rest: the related-objects read the claim amendment 6974061928 splits into PR 2.
- **File surface.** All 8 files are inside the amended claim surface. `packages/spec` is unchanged.

### Read at the head

- **The rule, at rule level.** Every object a new read shape reaches is judged by the MCP read guard exactly as the named object, and a refusal refuses the whole call before any record is read.
  - For `expand`, the queried object has already passed the guard. Each name is judged against that object's definition as the caller is served it, then every target goes through the guard, and only then is the one query run.
  - For `related`, every child goes through the guard first. Then each link field is judged against the child as served. Then the record is read, and only then the lists, so no list is read for a record the caller cannot see.
  - No caller filter reaches a list. The `related` entry schema is strict and has no `where`. A list's `where` is the link to the record alone, with `$contains` for a multi-value link.
  - Each list is capped at 20, and never above the door's page cap. A probe row gives `truncated: true` through the shared `servedQueryPage`.
- **Under the caller's security.**
  - On HTTP, the expanded names go through `findData`, with the existing expand gates and the engine's one batched expansion per field.
  - The stdio bridge builds the same map: a non-reference name is `INVALID_FIELD`, and a target that does not serve `get` is withheld.
  - Each list is an ordinary `bridge.query` of the child as the caller, so its `fields`/`orderBy` meet that read's own gates.
  - The record and each list carry `withheldFields` from #35179's helper, per row set.
- **The declared 404.** A related object whose definition is not served to the caller is refused `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` before any record read. This matches the existing reading of an unserved object, and the changeset and docs both say it.
- **Docs and changeset, read sentence by sentence.** `connect-mcp.mdx` gains the section, and the changeset covers `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime`, both `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. That level is right: there are new optional arguments, and an answer without them is unchanged. Neither text carries M1's sentence. Each refusal and bound they state matches the code and a pin.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `ec227fc7b1`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 52 in total. 1 failed (M2), 17 still running, and the rest are `success` or `skipped`.

### Nits (none blocks)

- In `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, the header docblock's new parenthetical, "(`expand` is served here since #35145 …)", sits on two lines with no leading ` * `.

### Owed after the fix

- A delta L1 at the fixed head, once CI is green.
- Contract review (claim 6985686134) and landing, through the seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fb4501686231790f6339cb12d9b6a7d1ef0f1dde`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #35145 (body and all 7 comments: triage 6972038283, claim 6973844822, claim amendment 6974061928, the two regrades, the two os-dev-reports 6979530359 / 6985647470); PR #35225 (body, 8 files, net diff `origin/main...fb45016862`); the 52 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff widens the published MCP tool surface in four places, and adds one optional member to an exported interface. Each one, judged:

1. **`query_records` accepts `expand`** (`string[]`, 1 to 3, `QUERY_EXPAND_MAX_FIELDS`). **Right.**
   - Each name is checked against the queried object as the caller is served it (`servedObjectDefinitionOf`, which both bridges build from the caller's own object view, ADR-0106 D1). So a field hidden by field-level security cannot be expanded, and the refusal calls it "Unknown field", which reveals nothing about it.
   - Each target comes from `referenceTargetOf`. That is the same function `assertExpandTargetsExist`, `servedExpand` and the engine's expansion loop use, so the object the guard judges is the object the engine reads.
   - Each target then passes the same `readGuard` closure the top-level call passed. This happens in `judgeQueryExpand`, before `bridge.query`. A refusal is `PERMISSION_DENIED`/403 for the whole call.
   - The only thing read before the verdict is the already-guarded object's own served definition. No records are read.
   - Rows: the engine's existing expansion does one batched `id IN (...)` per field through `engine.find` with the caller's context. That keeps the target's tenant wall, RLS and field masking. The dogfood pin shows `crm_account.annual_revenue` still withheld inside an expanded account.
   - Depth: the call is one level. Dotted names fail the served-field check, and the names reach `findData` with no nested `expand`.
   - Combined with `latestPer`: also judged before the read.
2. **`get_record` accepts `related`** (1 to 3 strict entries `{object, field?, fields?, orderBy?, limit?}`). **Right.**
   - Every child goes through `readGuard` first, all of them before anything about any child is read, its definition included (`judgeRelatedLists`).
   - The link field is then checked against the child as the caller is served it, and must point at the parent. A link hidden by field-level security cannot be followed.
   - Caller input matches the amendment 6974061928: `.strict()` on each entry and on `orderBy` items, no `where`, and the list's only filter is `relatedListWhere`, the link to the record's id.
   - Order of reads: the parent record is read first, so a parent the caller cannot see answers `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` and no list is read.
   - Each list is read like `query_records`: `bridge.query` as the caller. It carries the child's tenant wall, RLS and field-level judgement (sort keys included), plus `withheldFields` from `withheldFieldsFor(child, fields)`. Dogfood pins the RLS-hidden deal, the two-org wall and the withheld fields.
3. **Cap and `truncated` on related lists.** **Right.**
   - `relatedMaxRows = min(20, maxLimit)`. Zod `.max(relatedMaxRows)` refuses a larger limit at the door, and `judgeRelatedLists` clamps again.
   - Each list uses a limit+1 probe when `queryPageProbeFits`. Otherwise it uses the door's `hasMore`.
   - Both paths go through the shared `servedQueryPage`, so `truncated: true` is the same key and the same rule as `query_records`. Pinned: 25 rows answer 20 with `truncated`, and `limit: 5` is pinned too.
4. **`McpDataBridge.query` gains an optional `expand?: string[]`.** **Right.** The member is optional, so third-party bridges still compile. One that ignores it answers stored ids, which is declared.
   - HTTP bridge (`runtime/domains/mcp.ts`): forwards the names into `findData`, which lowers and gates them as REST does.
   - stdio bridge (`stdioExpandMap`): builds the expansion the way the data door does. A non-reference name is `INVALID_FIELD`. A target from a disabled package, or one that does not serve `get`, is withheld and keeps its stored id, as `servedExpand` does. The tool-level guard has already judged every target on this transport too.
5. **Declared deviation: a related object the caller lacks object permission on answers `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`/404, not `PERMISSION_DENIED`.** **Accepted.**
   - It is fail-closed: `servedObjectDefinitionOf` is null, and the refusal comes while relations are judged, before any record read.
   - It answers the same way the caller's served schema already answers a missing object (#35138), and it says less than a 403 would.
   - The MCP read guard itself still refuses with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, as the amendment requires.
   - The companion note is consistent with this: an `expand` target the engine refuses for object permission keeps the stored id, which is existing engine behaviour and leaks nothing.

Findings. None is must-fix.
- **should-fix (follow-up).** Related lists carry `total` but not the ADR-0090 D10 delegation-narrowing statement that `query_records` attaches (`diagnoseDelegation`). The rows are still narrowed by the engine, so this is the honest-count notice and not a row bound. Plain `get_record` carries none on `main` either.
- **nit.** A list's refusal renders `recordReadErrorResult(..., [])`, so the entry's own `fields`/`orderBy` names are not reported as not-recorded alongside the refusal.
- **nit.** Records nested under `expand` stay masked but carry no per-target `withheldFields`. This is declared in Acceptance notes. The tool description could say so.
- **nit.** The PR body's 维护者速读 says the unit file has 25 tests; the Tests section and the report say 26.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is `@objectstack/mcp: patch` and `@objectstack/runtime: patch`. These are the only two published packages the diff moves; `content/docs` and the dogfood tests do not publish. With `Metadata-protocol: none` and `@objectstack/spec` unchanged, AGENTS.md's level rule says a non-protocol change ships `patch`, so `patch` is **right**. It matches PR 1 (#35199).
- Both declaration lines appear in the PR body and in the changeset body.
- Clause-②: yes (widening) — **confirmed.** Only optional inputs and one optional interface member are added. Calls without `expand` or `related` are byte-identical (control pins in both suites). Nothing is narrowed or renamed, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]`. `security_findings`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, the deviation in ① item 5: answered, accepted.
- Dev flag, a third-party bridge that ignores `expand`: answered. This is a declared limit and fails safe (ids only).
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): **no finding.**
  - `expand` uses the engine's existing one-batched-read-per-field path. The reason is stated: each target's own permissions, RLS and FLS on one expansion path. This diff adds no new id materialisation.
  - `related` makes one pushed-down list read per child, filtered by a single parent id, plus the door's existing count. There is no in-app join, and no id set is materialised.
- Gate verdict, **escalated to the seat, not a contract finding:** `PR-body guards` is red on this head. The failing check is `check:closing-target-claim`: "PR #35225 closes #35145 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/issue-35145-mcp-related-read`". The card's claim and amendment name `claude/issue-35145-mcp-latest-per-and-related-read`. The fix is a claim amendment on the card naming this branch; no code changes.
- Gate verdict, still open: at read time, the Test Core shards, Build Core, Build Docs, the Type Check jobs and several Lint jobs were `in_progress`. Landing waits for their conclusions.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35145-mcp-related-read`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbaX2qDxUq9sF93EqqL`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**L1 delta · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `977e416ad0a93972e380cd100c297e191a878c73` · card #35145 (`Fixes #35145`, PR 2 of 2) · delta `fb450168..977e416a`, answering 6985771362 · read 2026-11-18T18:40Z

### What the delta changes

The delta has two commits of this PR's own and one merge of main (`3e4d531d8f`, which brought #35222, #35226 and #35227, none of them touching this PR's files). The PR's net diff is now 9 files, +1259 / -8.

- **M1 is fixed.** The `query_records` text now says that a field whose object this door does not serve refuses the call. A record the caller may not read on a served object is not expanded, and the field keeps its stored id. `connect-mcp.mdx` and the changeset say the same in the same terms. The new dogfood pin expands `crm_activity.contact` onto `crm_contact`, which the member may not read, in the same call as `account`. The call is answered, `contact` holds its stored id, no contact field value appears anywhere in the payload, and `account` comes back expanded.
- **M2 is fixed.** `PR-body guards` is green against claim 6985788194.
- **The docblock nit is fixed.** The two lines in `stdio-data-bridge.ts` carry their ` * ` again.
- **Added for the L2 should-fix.** Each related list now carries the delegation-narrowing notice `query_records` carries, through the same `withDelegationNotice`, when the agent ceiling narrowed that list's read. The probe is caught, so a failing diagnosis never fails the list. Two unit pins cover it: a narrowed list next to an unnarrowed one, and a probe that throws. The changeset and docs name the notice.
- **A declared step outside the claimed surface.** `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` classifies the two new `referenceTargetOf` callers: `stdio-data-bridge.ts` as decided in `stdioExpandMap`, and `mcp-relation-reads.ts` as executing through the data door. Each classification matches the code I read. It is a test-only pin roster, and the pin had to name them, so I read this as a deviation needed to make CI green, not a scope change.

### Read at the head

- The full L1 at `fb450168` (6985771362) stands for everything else. That covers the read-guard rule on every target before any read, no caller filter on a related list, the 20-row cap with `truncated`, `withheldFields` per row set, the declared 404, and `Fixes`.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `02a1e2f29c`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 74 in total, all completed, none failed (62 `success`, 12 `skipped`).

### Not mine, still owed

- The L2 delta at this head (claim 6988022910), then landing through the seat. #35193 also moves `stdio-data-bridge.ts` (the `Symbol.for` constants above `unwrapRows`), so whichever of the two PRs lands second merges main.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `977e416ad0a93972e380cd100c297e191a878c73`
Local-runs: none

Delta over the PASS 6985818359 at `fb45016862`. Inputs read: card #35145 (body and every comment, including claim 6985788194 and the delta os-dev-report 6987956358); PR #35225 (the updated body, 9 files, and the PR's own change between `fb45016862` and this head, restricted to the PR's files); the L1 REWORK 6985771362 and the prior PASS; the 74 check-runs on this head.

Shape of the delta: two PR commits (`3d6e7691fee`, `0e7914f180e`) and one merge of `origin/main` (`977e416ad0a`). The merge changes none of the PR's 9 files, and the three `main` commits it brings in (`#35222`, `#35227`, `#35226`) touch none of them either, so it resolved no conflict. The PR's own delta is 7 files, +84 / -10. `mcp-relation-reads.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` are unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`query_records` tool text for `expand`.** **Right.**
   - The text now says: "A field whose object this door does not serve you refuses the call; a record you may not read on a served object is not expanded, and the field keeps its stored id."
   - The first clause uses the read guard's own words. `judgeTarget` refuses with "reaches object '…', which this door does not serve you", as `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, before any read.
   - The second clause is what the engine does. `expandRelatedRecords` reads each target through `this.find` with the caller's context. A refused sub-read is caught, and the bare FK id is kept. A row the target's row policy hides is missing from the id map, so the field falls back to the stored id.
   - On HTTP, `servedExpand` withholds a target that does not serve `get`. On stdio, `stdioExpandMap` does the same with `continue`. Both keep the id.
   - Pinned in the dogfood suite. `crm_activity.contact` points at `crm_contact`, which the guard admits but the member may not read; the armed control shows contacts are unreadable. The call is answered, `contact` equals the stored id, no contact data appears, and `account` on the same row still expands.
   - The docs and the changeset say the same. The docs also name the hidden-row case.
2. **Delegation-narrowing notice on each related list.** **Right.** This closes the prior should-fix.
   - Each list runs `bridge.diagnoseDelegation(plan.object)` with a catch that turns a failure into no answer, and adds `withDelegationNotice` only when the result is narrowed and carries a statement. That is the same guard and the same helper `query_records` uses, so the notice is the same `delegationNarrowed` / `warning` pair.
   - The diagnosis is keyed on the child object, which is the object the list reads. It runs after the list read, so it cannot fail the list or change which rows it holds.
   - Two unit pins. A narrowed list carries the notice, a sibling list does not, and a plain `query_records` gives the same answer. A diagnosis that throws still answers the list.
3. **The two new `referenceTargetOf` callers in `second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`.**
   - **`stdio-data-bridge.ts` as `decided` / `get` (`stdioExpandMap`): true.**
     - This is the file's only arbiter call (line 333).
     - The function asks `canServeApiOperation(declared?.enable, 'get')` on the target before adding it to the expand map. The file imports the decision from `@objectstack/spec/data`.
     - The wiring call `stdioExpandMap(reads, object` exists (line 1473).
     - The named pin (`mcp-relation-reads.test.ts`, its stdio block) holds a target with `apiEnabled: false` withheld.
     - The `get` operation matches the data door's `servesExpansionTarget` row.
   - **`mcp-relation-reads.ts` as `executes`, decided in `protocol-query-validation.ts`: true in substance, with a nit.**
     - The file's arbiter calls (`targetOf`, used by `judgeQueryExpand` and the related-link checks) read no record. They only name the object to ask the MCP guard, and check that a link points at the parent. The `also` text says so.
     - On the HTTP bridge, `findData` reads the expansion, and `servedExpand` / `servesExpansionTarget` decides it.
     - Nit: the `read` and `also` wording describe the HTTP path only. On stdio, the expansion is decided in `stdioExpandMap` (its own `decided` row, above), and each list goes through the stdio bridge's `query`, not `findData`. The pin's invariant still holds, because every path reaches a classified decided door. Only the prose is narrower than the code.
4. **The earlier ① judgments still hold.** The delta leaves the guard, the judging order, `judgeRelatedLists`, the cap and probe, `servedQueryPage`, both bridges' `expand` and the declared `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` deviation untouched. The only `mcp-http-tools.ts` changes are the description string and the per-list notice.

Prior findings, re-judged:
- should-fix (delegation notice): closed by item 2.
- nit (unit-test count): closed. The body says 28 everywhere, which matches the delta report.
- nit (a list refusal renders `recordReadErrorResult(..., [])`): open, still a nit.
- nit (no per-target `withheldFields` under `expand`): open, still a nit. It is declared in Acceptance notes.

New findings. None is must-fix.
- **nit.** The pin's `mcp-relation-reads.ts` row describes the HTTP path only (item 3).
- **nit.** The changeset's `expand` bullet says "Only the read guard's refusal refuses the call". That is true of target objects, but `INVALID_FIELD` / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` also refuse. The next bullet states them, so nothing contradicts it.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is unchanged in frontmatter: `@objectstack/mcp: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`. Only its body gains two sentences, and both match the code.
- The new core file is a repo test pin, which does not publish, so no `@objectstack/core` entry is owed. `Check Changeset` is success.
- `patch` is still **right**: `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `@objectstack/spec` is unchanged.
- Clause-②: yes (widening) is **still confirmed**.
